Get started

Introduction to multiCollglm

Examples

Real-data applications. Start with the overview, which links to each example and summarizes the four condition-number definitions on all the data sets.

Examples: real-data applications

Index of the worked examples of multiCollglm: five reproductions of published collinearity diagnostics on real data, and a comparison with the VisCollin package, with a summary of the four condition-number definitions on every data set.

Reproduction: cancer remission data (Lee 1974)

Reproduces the three logistic-model variants fitted to Lee’s (1974) cancer remission dataset – Lesaffre and Marx (1993), Ozkale and Arican (2016)/Ozkale (2021), and Huang, Jou and Cho (2015) – and contrasts them against multiCollglm’s four methods (WS, MP, X, RAW).

Reproduction: Chatterjee and Hadi (1988) -- Nitrogen data

Reproduces the collinearity diagnostic of the Nitrogen dataset (Gamma, inverse link), contrasts it against nine published reproductions/variants, and shows how multiCollglm’s four condition-number methods (WS, MP, X, RAW) behave, and why centering the weighted matrix is not possible for this model.

Reproduction: coal mine roof-fracture data (Mine)

Reproduces the collinearity diagnostic of the coal mine roof-fracture dataset, used by five works fitting different count-data GLMs, and shows that the “RAW” (untransformed) method exactly reproduces the most-cited value in the literature.

Reproduction: Bodyfat data (TH.data)

Reproduces the collinearity diagnostic of the bodyfat dataset (Gamma, log link) used by five works, and documents a structural fact about the log link for the Gamma family that explains why three of the package’s methods coincide exactly in this case.

Reproduction: plastic plywood manufacturing data (Plastic)

Reproduces the collinearity diagnostic of the plastic plywood manufacturing dataset, used by six works fitting different count-data GLMs, and documents a citation error (CN = 8634.73) that propagates unverified across at least three publications.

Comparison with other software

How multiCollglm relates to the VisCollin package, on the same data.

Comparison with VisCollin

Compares multiCollglm with the VisCollin package (Friendly), on the real datasets of the package: what VisCollin::colldiag() computes when it is given a GLM, when it coincides exactly with multiCollglm (method = “X”), and where the two diverge (IRLS weights, factors, weights and offsets, visualization).
